vulnerabilities.name: Missing Security Header: Content-Security-Policy
vulnerabilities.remediation: Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header allows a broader attack surface for injection-based attacks such as XSS.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing Security Header: Strict-Transport-Security
vulnerabilities.remediation: Missing HTTP Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header exposes users to SSL-stripping / downgrade attacks.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing Security Header: X-Content-Type-Options
vulnerabilities.remediation: Missing X-Content-Type-Options header allows browsers to MIME-sniff responses, which can lead to content-type confusion attacks.

vulnerabilities.name: Potentially Unsafe HTTP Methods Exposed
vulnerabilities.remediation: Disable unused HTTP methods (e.g. PUT, DELETE, TRACE) at the web server or framework routing layer unless explicitly required and properly authorized.

findings.title: Potential BOLA/IDOR exposure on GET /page/news/65
evidence: Path contains an object identifier segment: /page/news/65
safe_poc_steps: Manually review whether object ownership is enforced server-side for this identifier.
No authorization bypass was attempted automatically.
findings.impact: If ownership checks are missing, an authenticated user could access or modify objects belonging to other users by changing the identifier.
remediation: Enforce server-side object ownership checks on every request that accepts an object identifier.
Prefer indirect, non-guessable references (e.g. per-user opaque tokens) over sequential IDs.
findings.false_positive_notes: Automatically flagged from public path/query structure only; no authenticated requests, tokens, or credentials were used, and no request testing was performed.
